_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Morocco is the second of three North Africa countries researched this session (AF/G.9 priority 1) -- Algeria and Tunisia alongside it. Researched by a subagent this session against the branch's full Research.1.md discipline, reading HCP's own methodological note directly plus the full 19-article text of the 2021 social-protection framework law. Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review, following the established DRAFT-then-import pattern.
_note: Morocco's CPI methodology note is the most self-documenting of the three North Africa countries researched this session: it names COICOP (without a version), states its release calendar follows the IMF's SDDS (independently confirmed by the IMF's own 2022 Morocco SDDS Annual Observance Report, which lists 'Price index: Consumer prices' as an SDDS-monitored category), and states its missing-price imputation method follows 'le manuel du FMI' -- the only country in this batch whose own CPI document names an IMF manual directly, even without a full title. On social protection, Morocco shows the same 'real mechanism, not CPI-based' shape already found for Rwanda's actuarial trigger and Uganda's Minister-set NSSF rate: the CMR's civil-service pension statute (Loi 011-71, Art. 44 bis) automatically ties pension increases to the civil-service base-salary scale, and the CNSS's founding statute (Dahir 1-72-184, Art. 68) ties discretionary pension revaluation to a wage-level gap -- both real, both statutory, neither CPI-linked. The 2021 social-protection framework law (Loi-cadre 09-21), read in full across all 19 articles, uses the aspirational phrase 'soutenir le pouvoir d'achat des familles' twice but specifies no indexation formula, trigger, or review cycle anywhere.

_open_questions.question: HCP's methodological note names 'COICOP' as the CPI's classification but never states a version (no 'COICOP 2018' anywhere in the document, and no web search for 'HCP Maroc COICOP 2018' surfaced one). The `un-coicop-2018` edge below should be treated as version-unconfirmed pending a document that states the vintage explicitly.

Loi n° 58-23 (establishing Morocco's Aide Sociale Directe direct cash-support programme) exists on ANSS's own site only as a non-OCR'd Arabic-language scan; no French version could be located. Whether the law itself contains any inflation/CPI-adjustment provision is genuinely unconfirmed, not a documented silence -- official secondary sources (ANSS's own site, the government portal maroc.ma) describe benefit increases as driven by budget sustainability and the 'Chantier Royal' rollout schedule, not inflation, but this is not a reading of the statute itself.

A trade-association news article (CGEM) attributes a 2020 CNSS pension-revalorisation decree to 'l'article 9' of Dahir 1-72-184, but Article 9 as read this session governs the fund's conseil d'administration, not pensions -- the substantively relevant provision is Article 68. Possibly a citation error in the secondary source; not resolved this session.

reports.title: Indice des Prix à la Consommation (IPC), Base 100 : 2017
reports.description: Morocco's official monthly Consumer Price Index. VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session via HCP's own methodological note. 'Le premier IPC basé sur la nouvelle référence 100 : 2017 a été publié le 27 avril de l'année 2020.' Formula: 'une formule de Laspeyres en chaîne combinée à une moyenne géométrique pour le premier niveau d'agrégation.' Classification: 'classifiés selon la nomenclature COICOP' (version unstated -- see _open_questions). Missing-price imputation: 'la méthode d'imputation est appliquée conformément au manuel du FMI, sauf pour les produits dont les prix sont fixés par l'État... où la méthode du report est utilisée.' Release calendar: 'conformément au calendrier établi selon les normes spéciales de diffusion des données (NSDD)' -- the French name for the IMF's SDDS.

release_schedule.rule: Per HCP's official Calendrier des publications (embedded Google Sheets calendar), the Indice des Prix à la Consommation (IPC) is published Mensuelle (monthly), with reference release day of the 20th, 21st, or 22nd of the month following the reference period ("Référence: 20, 21 ou 22").
release_schedule.note: The stated rule gives a range (20th-22nd) rather than one fixed day; actual 2026 editions were consistently released on the 22nd of the following month (April 2026 data released 22/04/2026, May 2026 data released 22/05/2026, June 2026 data released 22/07/2026), so 2026-08-22 (for July 2026 data) is used as the computed next date. Source calendar: https://www.hcp.ma/Calendrier-des-publications_r630.html

reports.title: Enquête nationale sur les dépenses et la consommation des ménages (2013-2014)
reports.description: The national household expenditure and consumption survey named by HCP as 'la principale source' of the CPI's expenditure weights, supplemented for the rent group by the 2014 General Population and Housing Census and for pharmaceuticals by 2016 drug-expenditure data.

reports.title: Loi n° 011-71 instituant un régime de pensions civiles (Chapitre II bis : Revalorisation, Article 44 bis)
reports.publisher: Caisse Marocaine des Retraites (CMR) / Trésorerie Générale du Royaume
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session (consolidated text hosted by the Trésorerie Générale du Royaume). Article 44 bis, inserted by Loi n° 06-89: 'Les pensions de retraite et les pensions d'ayants cause concédées au titre de la présente loi sont majorées de toute augmentation affectant le traitement de base afférent aux grade, échelle et échelon ou classe effectivement détenus à la date de radiation des cadres.' A real, mandatory ('sont majorées') indexation mechanism -- but tied to the civil-service base-salary scale, not to CPI or inflation.

reports.title: Dahir portant loi n° 1-72-184 relatif au régime de sécurité sociale
reports.publisher: Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS), Morocco
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session. Founding statute of Morocco's private-sector social security fund. Article 68: 'Lorsque l'écart entre le niveau des salaires sur la base desquels ont été liquidées les pensions d'invalidité, de vieillesse et de survivants et le niveau des salaires en cours le justifie, ces pensions peuvent être revalorisées par décret pris sur proposition du ministre chargé du travail.' A real but discretionary ('peuvent être') mechanism, triggered by a wage-level gap, not a price index.

reports.title: Loi-cadre n° 09-21 relative à la protection sociale
reports.publisher: Royaume du Maroc / Chef du Gouvernement
reports.description: VERIFIED DIRECTLY this session -- full text (Articles 1-19) read via Bulletin Officiel n° 7132 du 6 octobre 2022. Morocco's 2021 framework law for generalizing social protection (AMO, family allocations, pension coverage, unemployment benefit) over a five-year rollout. Uses the aspirational phrase 'soutenir le pouvoir d'achat des familles' twice (Préambule; Article 4, on the flat-rate family allocations) but specifies no indexation formula, trigger, or review cycle anywhere in the law.

reports.title: Loi n° 58-23 relative au régime de l'aide sociale directe
reports.publisher: Agence Nationale du Soutien Social (ANSS) / Royaume du Maroc
reports.description: Statute establishing Morocco's direct cash-support programme (Aide Sociale Directe). Primary text available on ANSS's own site only as a non-OCR'd Arabic scan -- could not be read this session (see _open_questions). Official secondary sources (ANSS's own announcements; the government portal maroc.ma) describe recent benefit increases as driven by 'la mise en œuvre progressive du Chantier Royal' and 'la soutenabilité budgétaire du régime', not by inflation or CPI, but this is not a verified reading of the statute itself.

dependencies.basis: HCP methodological note: 'La principale source de ces pondérations est l'enquête nationale sur les dépenses et la consommation des ménages (2013-2014).'

HCP methodological note: 'la méthode d'imputation est appliquée conformément au manuel du FMI' -- Morocco's missing-price imputation procedure is explicitly stated to follow the IMF's manual, though the document does not give the manual's exact title. Narrow scope (imputation only), noted in the node's own description.
HCP methodological note: 'classifiés selon la nomenclature COICOP.' CAVEAT: no version number is stated anywhere in the document -- see ma-coicop-version-unconfirmed.

HCP methodological note: 'conformément au calendrier établi selon les normes spéciales de diffusion des données (NSDD)' -- Morocco's own document states its CPI release calendar follows SDDS. Corroborated by the IMF's own 'Morocco: Annual Observance Report of the Special Data Dissemination Standard for 2022': 'Morocco subscribed to the SDDS on December 15, 2005 and met all SDDS requirements at the time of subscription,' listing 'Price index: Consumer prices' as an SDDS-monitored, monthly category.

Loi n° 011-71, Article 44 bis, ties pension increases to increases in the civil-service base salary scale ('traitement de base'), not to any price index.
Dahir 1-72-184, Article 68, ties discretionary pension revalorisation to a gap between the wage level at pension liquidation and current wage levels, not to the price level or CPI.

Complete text of Loi-cadre n° 09-21 (Articles 1-19) read directly; contains no indexation, revalorisation, or CPI/inflation-adjustment provision anywhere. Uses only the aspirational phrase 'soutenir le pouvoir d'achat des familles' with no operational mechanism attached.

Could not access readable primary text of Loi n° 58-23 (Arabic-only scanned PDF, no OCR available this session). Secondary/official sources describe recent increases as driven by the 'Chantier Royal' rollout and budget sustainability, with no mention of inflation or CPI -- but this is not a verified reading of the statute itself, so treated as unresolved rather than a confirmed denial.
